title: How Much Does Botox Cost in Florida? (2026 Price Guide)

sections: How Botox pricing works

Clinics charge per unit. A frown-line treatment commonly uses about 20 units; forehead lines and crow's-feet add more, so two people can pay very different totals at the same per-unit price. Ask how many units a provider recommends and who performs the injection.
What changes your price

Injector experience, the number of areas treated, the product used (Botox, Dysport or Xeomin), and any current promotions. For a medical injectable, the cheapest quote is not automatically the best choice.

title: Botox vs Dysport vs Xeomin: Differences, Cost and How to Choose
lede: Botox, Dysport and Xeomin are all botulinum-toxin type-A injectables that soften dynamic wrinkles. They all work; they differ in dosing, spread, and onset speed, not in whether they are effective.
sections: The key differences

Dysport units are not 1:1 with Botox units and it tends to spread a little more, useful for larger areas like the forehead. Xeomin is a purified formulation. Onset is roughly 2 to 4 days for Dysport and 3 to 7 days for Botox and Xeomin; all last about 3 to 4 months.
Cost comparison
Because unit counts differ between products, per-unit price is misleading. Always compare the total quoted for your treatment, not the sticker per-unit rate.
How to choose
Pick the injector first and the product second. An experienced provider recommends a product based on your treatment area and history.
faqs: Is Dysport cheaper than Botox?
Sometimes per unit, but Dysport typically uses more units, so compare total cost.
Which one lasts the longest?
All last roughly 3 to 4 months; duration depends more on dose and metabolism than brand.

title: Lip Filler vs Botox: What's the Difference and Which Do You Need?
lede: Lip filler and Botox are different tools for different jobs. Lip filler adds volume and shape using hyaluronic acid; Botox is a muscle-relaxing injectable that softens wrinkles caused by movement. Many people confuse them, but they treat different concerns.
sections: What each one does

Lip filler (an HA product like Juvederm or Restylane) plumps and defines the lips by adding volume. Botox (a botulinum-toxin injectable) relaxes specific muscles to smooth dynamic lines such as frown lines and crow's-feet. A 'lip flip' is a small Botox technique that gently everts the upper lip — it is not the same as adding filler volume.
How long they last
HA lip filler typically lasts about 6 to 18 months. Botox usually lasts about 3 to 4 months. Because Botox wears off faster, it needs more frequent touch-ups.
Cost and choosing

Filler is priced per syringe; Botox is priced per unit — so the two are not directly comparable on price. Pick your goal first: more volume and shape means filler; softening movement wrinkles means Botox. An experienced injector can combine both when it makes sense.
faqs: Can you get lip filler and Botox at the same time?
Yes, providers often combine them, for example filler for lip volume plus a Botox lip flip. Discuss your goals at a consultation.
Which is cheaper, Botox or lip filler?
They are priced differently (units vs syringes) and treat different things, so compare total treatment cost, not sticker rates.

title: How Long Does Lip Filler Last? What to Expect
h1: How long does lip filler last?
lede: Most hyaluronic-acid lip fillers last about 6 to 18 months, with many people seeing results hold for roughly 9 to 12 months before a touch-up. How long yours lasts depends on the product, your metabolism, and how much was placed.
sections: Typical timeline

After the initial swelling settles (usually one to two weeks), your final result appears. HA lip filler then gradually breaks down over months. Smaller amounts and faster metabolisms tend to fade sooner; larger placements can last longer.
What affects how long it lasts

The filler brand and formulation, how much product was used, your metabolism and activity level, and how the area moves all influence longevity. Lips are highly mobile, so lip filler often fades a bit faster than filler in less-active areas.
Maintaining your results

Many people schedule a touch-up once or twice a year. HA fillers can also be dissolved with hyaluronidase if you want to reverse or adjust them. A qualified injector can recommend a maintenance schedule.
faqs: Does lip filler last longer the more you get it?
Some people find results hold a little longer with repeat treatments, but this varies. Longevity depends mostly on product, dose, and metabolism.
Can lip filler be dissolved early?
Yes. HA lip filler can be dissolved with an enzyme called hyaluronidase if you want to reverse it.

title: How Long Does Botox Last? What to Expect
lede: Botox typically lasts about 3 to 4 months. First-time patients sometimes notice it wears off a little sooner, and results can vary with the dose, the area treated, and your metabolism.
sections: Typical timeline

Botox usually starts working within 3 to 7 days and reaches full effect around two weeks. The muscle-relaxing result then gradually fades over roughly 3 to 4 months as the product wears off and movement returns.
What affects how long it lasts

The number of units used, the specific muscle treated, your metabolism, and how expressive the area is all matter. Under-dosing to save money often means results fade faster, so the cheapest treatment is not always the best value.
Keeping results consistent

Many people book touch-ups every 3 to 4 months to maintain a smooth look. Staying on a regular schedule can help results look consistent over time. Your injector can recommend a cadence based on how you respond.
faqs: Does Botox last longer over time?
Some regular patients find they need slightly less product or fewer sessions over time, but the typical duration stays around 3 to 4 months.
Why did my Botox wear off quickly?
Lower doses, a very active muscle, or a faster metabolism can shorten how long it lasts. Discuss dosing with your injector.

title: How Long Does Microneedling Last? Results and Timeline
lede: A single microneedling session gives a fresh, glowing look that often lasts several weeks, while the collagen-building benefits keep developing for months. Most providers recommend a series of sessions for longer-lasting results.
sections: What to expect after one session

In the days to weeks after microneedling, skin can look brighter and smoother as it heals. This initial glow commonly lasts around 4 to 6 weeks. Underneath, the treatment stimulates collagen, which keeps improving skin texture over the following months.
How long the results last

Because microneedling works by building collagen, results are cumulative. A course of about 3 to 6 sessions spaced a few weeks apart tends to produce the most noticeable, longer-lasting improvement — often holding for several months. Many people maintain results with a session every 6 to 12 months.
What affects longevity
Your skin concern, skincare routine, sun protection, and whether you complete a full series all affect how long results last. Consistent sun protection helps preserve the improvement.
faqs: Is one microneedling session enough?
One session gives a temporary glow, but most providers recommend a series of 3 to 6 for lasting collagen-building results.
How often should you get microneedling?
A common approach is an initial series a few weeks apart, then maintenance every 6 to 12 months depending on your goals.

title: Microneedling vs Chemical Peel: Differences, Downtime and How to Choose
lede: Microneedling and chemical peels treat many of the same concerns — texture, tone, fine lines, acne scarring — but they work on different layers of the skin. Microneedling rebuilds collagen from underneath, while a peel resurfaces from the top. The right choice depends on your specific concern.
sections: How each treatment works

Microneedling uses a pen or roller tipped with fine needles to create controlled micro-injuries in the skin. Your body responds by producing new collagen and elastin, which is why it is often called collagen induction therapy. A chemical peel takes the opposite route: a provider applies an acid solution — commonly glycolic, salicylic, or TCA — that exfoliates the outer layers so smoother, more even skin surfaces as it heals.
Which one fits which concern

Microneedling is generally the stronger choice for pitted or rolling acne scars, enlarged pores, fine lines, and mild skin laxity, because it works beneath the surface. Chemical peels tend to do better on surface-level concerns: sun spots, uneven tone, melasma, post-acne discoloration, and overall dullness.
Downtime and sessions

Microneedling downtime is usually 1 to 3 days of redness similar to a mild sunburn, and most providers recommend a series of 3 to 6 sessions spaced 4 to 6 weeks apart. Light chemical peels involve little to no downtime and can be repeated every 4 to 6 weeks; medium and deep peels can require 7 to 14 days of visible peeling and recovery.
What they cost

Published prices for both treatments commonly fall in the $200 to $700 per session range, depending on the provider, the depth of the treatment, and any add-ons. Your total also depends on how many sessions your plan calls for, so compare quotes on the full series rather than a single session.
Can you combine them?

Yes — many providers alternate microneedling and light peels in the same treatment plan, since they target different layers of the skin. Spacing between treatments matters, so the schedule should come from a licensed provider rather than stacking them on your own.
faqs: Which is better for acne scars?
For pitted or rolling scars, microneedling usually wins because it remodels tissue below the surface. For flat discoloration left after breakouts, a peel is often the better fit.
Is microneedling or a chemical peel more painful?
Both are tolerable for most people. Microneedling is done with topical numbing; light peels sting briefly during application. Deeper peels involve more discomfort and longer recovery.

title: How Often Should You Get a HydraFacial? A Realistic Schedule
h1: How often should you get a HydraFacial?
lede: For most people, a HydraFacial every 4 to 6 weeks is the sweet spot — it lines up with the skin's roughly 28-day cell turnover cycle. Some skin concerns benefit from a shorter interval at first, but going more often than every 2 weeks is generally not recommended.
sections: The standard schedule

Skin renews itself on an approximately 28-day cycle, which is why most providers recommend a HydraFacial about once a month, or every 4 to 6 weeks. On that cadence each session maintains the exfoliation, hydration and glow of the last one instead of starting from scratch.
When a shorter interval helps

For active breakouts or very oily skin, providers often start with a session every 2 to 3 weeks for the first couple of months to clear congestion, then stretch back to monthly maintenance. For hyperpigmentation or fine-line goals, every 3 to 4 weeks is a common starting rhythm. Your provider should tailor the plan to your skin rather than selling a fixed package.
Can you get one too often?

Yes. Because each session includes physical and chemical exfoliation, going more often than every 2 weeks risks over-exfoliating and irritating the skin barrier. More is not better here — consistency is what compounds.
If you only go occasionally

A single HydraFacial before an event still delivers a same-day glow that typically lasts a few weeks. If you go quarterly, expect a fresh reset each time rather than the cumulative improvement a monthly schedule builds.
faqs: How long do HydraFacial results last?
The visible glow and hydration from one session typically last around 4 to 6 weeks, which is exactly why monthly treatment is the standard recommendation.
Can I get a HydraFacial every 2 weeks?
Every 2 to 3 weeks is sometimes recommended short-term for acne-prone or congested skin, but more frequently than every 2 weeks risks over-exfoliation.
Is a monthly HydraFacial worth it?
If dullness, congestion or dryness are recurring concerns, monthly sessions maintain results continuously — and many med spas offer memberships that cut the per-session price.

title: HydraFacial vs Microneedling: Which Treatment Fits Your Skin?
lede: A HydraFacial polishes and hydrates the surface of your skin with zero downtime; microneedling rebuilds collagen underneath and needs a few days of recovery. They solve different problems — and many treatment plans use both.
sections: How each treatment works

A HydraFacial uses a vortex-suction device to cleanse, exfoliate, extract impurities and infuse hydrating serums in a single non-invasive session. Microneedling takes the opposite approach: fine sterile needles create controlled micro-injuries that trigger the skin's healing response, producing new collagen and elastin over the following weeks and months.
Which concern each one fits

Choose a HydraFacial for surface-level goals: dullness, dryness, congested pores, blackheads, mild texture and an instant pre-event glow. Choose microneedling for structural goals: pitted acne scars, deeper texture irregularities, fine lines, and mild laxity — RF microneedling adds a skin-tightening effect. If your concern lives below the surface, no amount of surface polishing will fix it.
Downtime and comfort

A HydraFacial is painless with no downtime — most people go straight back to their day with an immediate glow. Microneedling involves topical numbing, a prickly sensation during treatment, and 24 to 72 hours of redness similar to a mild sunburn.
Cost comparison

Published HydraFacial prices in Florida commonly run $150 to $350 per session depending on tier. Standard microneedling typically runs $200 to $400 per session, with RF microneedling or PRP add-ons pushing $400 to $800. Microneedling is usually sold as a series of 3 to 6 sessions, so compare full-plan costs, not single sessions.
Using both together

Many providers combine them: a HydraFacial to deep-clean and hydrate, then microneedling a few weeks later for collagen remodeling — or monthly HydraFacials between microneedling series. The sequencing matters, so let a licensed provider set the schedule.
faqs: Is a HydraFacial better than microneedling?
Neither is better — they target different layers. HydraFacial wins for instant surface glow and hydration; microneedling wins for scars, deeper texture and long-term collagen.
Can you do a HydraFacial and microneedling on the same day?
Most providers space them apart rather than stacking them the same day, since one exfoliates the surface and the other creates micro-injuries. Ask your provider how to sequence them.
Which lasts longer?
HydraFacial results fade over about 4 to 6 weeks. Microneedling results build for months after a series and can last considerably longer, because the treatment creates new collagen.

title: Chemical Peel vs Microdermabrasion: Differences, Downtime and How to Choose
lede: Chemical peels and microdermabrasion both exfoliate the skin to improve tone and texture, but they do it in completely different ways. Microdermabrasion physically buffs away the surface with no downtime; a chemical peel uses acids to dissolve dead skin and can reach deeper. The right choice depends on your concern and how much recovery time you can spare.
sections: How each treatment works

Microdermabrasion is mechanical exfoliation — a diamond-tip or crystal wand sands off the outermost layer of the epidermis. A chemical peel is chemical exfoliation: a provider applies an acid solution — glycolic, lactic or salicylic for light peels, TCA for medium ones — that triggers a controlled shedding of skin layers. Microdermabrasion stays strictly superficial, while peels can be dialed from light to deep.
Which concern each one fits

Microdermabrasion suits mild, surface-level goals: dullness, rough texture, enlarged pores and a quick pre-event refresh, and it is gentle enough for sensitive skin that reacts poorly to acids. Chemical peels reach further, making them the stronger choice for stubborn hyperpigmentation, sun damage, melasma, post-acne discoloration and fine lines. For pitted acne scars or laxity, a collagen-building option like microneedling often beats both.
Downtime and frequency

Microdermabrasion has essentially no downtime — minor redness at most — and is typically repeated every two to four weeks. Light peels also involve little to no visible peeling and can be done roughly monthly, but medium and deep peels bring several days to a couple of weeks of flaking and redness and are spaced much further apart. Sun protection matters after either treatment, and especially after a peel.
How to choose

If you want a gentle, no-downtime glow and your concerns are mild, microdermabrasion is a reasonable start. If you are targeting pigmentation, sun damage or fine lines and can tolerate some peeling, a chemical peel usually delivers more. Many providers alternate the two across a treatment plan — a licensed provider can tell you which fits your skin.
faqs: Which is better for hyperpigmentation, a chemical peel or microdermabrasion?
A chemical peel is generally more effective for stubborn pigmentation, melasma and sun spots because it works deeper than microdermabrasion, which mainly refreshes the surface.
Is microdermabrasion or a chemical peel gentler?
Microdermabrasion is the gentler of the two, with no acids and essentially no downtime, which makes it a common choice for sensitive skin or a first treatment.
Can you do microdermabrasion and a chemical peel together?
Some providers combine or alternate them across a treatment plan, since they exfoliate differently. The sequencing should come from a licensed provider rather than doing both on your own.

title: Dermal Fillers vs Botox: What's the Difference and Which Do You Need?
lede: Dermal fillers and Botox are both injectables, but they do opposite jobs. Botox relaxes the muscles that cause expression lines; dermal fillers add volume to smooth folds and restore fullness. Many people use one, and plenty use both — the right choice depends on what you are trying to fix.
sections: How each one works

Botox is a neuromodulator: it temporarily relaxes the muscle under a wrinkle so the skin above it smooths out. Dermal fillers are gels — usually hyaluronic acid — injected to add volume beneath the skin. In short, Botox softens movement, fillers restore or add structure. They are not interchangeable, which is why injectors often use them in different areas of the same face.
Which concern each one fits

Botox is best for dynamic wrinkles caused by movement: forehead lines, frown lines between the brows, and crow's feet. Dermal fillers are best for static concerns and lost volume: flattened cheeks, a soft jawline, nasolabial folds, thin lips, and under-eye hollows. If a line is there when your face is completely still, filler is usually the tool; if it appears only when you move, Botox usually is.
Cost, results and how long they last

Botox is priced per unit and typically lasts about 3 to 4 months. Fillers are priced per syringe, cost more up front, and last longer — roughly 6 to 18 months depending on the product and placement. Botox takes a few days to show; filler results are largely immediate. Because they solve different problems, comparing them on price alone misses the point — the better question is which one addresses your concern.
Can you get both?

Yes, and many people do — a common combination is Botox for the upper face and filler for the cheeks, lips or jawline. A qualified injector can map which areas call for which, and sometimes stages them across visits. The decision should come from a licensed provider after assessing your face at rest and in motion.
faqs: Is Botox or filler better for forehead lines?
Botox is usually the better choice for forehead lines, because those are dynamic wrinkles caused by muscle movement, which Botox relaxes. Filler is aimed at volume loss and static folds instead.
Do dermal fillers last longer than Botox?
Yes. Botox typically lasts about 3 to 4 months, while most dermal fillers last from 6 to 18 months depending on the product and where it is placed.
Can you get Botox and fillers at the same time?
Often, yes — many injectors combine them in one visit, treating different areas. Whether to do both at once should be decided by a licensed provider based on your goals.

title: How Long Do Dermal Fillers Last? A Realistic Timeline by Type and Area
h1: How long do dermal fillers last?
lede: Most dermal fillers last somewhere between 6 and 18 months, but the real answer depends on the product used, where it is placed, and your own metabolism. Thin fillers in high-movement areas fade faster; firmer fillers in stable areas last longer.
sections: Typical timelines by product

Hyaluronic-acid fillers — the most common type — generally last 6 to 18 months. Lighter formulas used for lips or fine lines tend toward the shorter end, while firmer formulas built for cheeks and jawline hold longer. Calcium-hydroxylapatite fillers such as Radiesse often last around a year or more, and poly-L-lactic-acid (Sculptra), which stimulates your own collagen, can last two years or more as its effect builds gradually.
Why placement and movement matter

Filler breaks down faster in areas that move a lot. Lips, for example, are constantly in motion and metabolize filler quicker than the cheeks, which are relatively stable. Your metabolism, activity level and how much product was placed all play a role too — a fuller correction generally outlasts a light, conservative one.
Making results last

There is no need to wait until filler fully disappears; many injectors recommend a smaller touch-up before it is completely gone to keep results consistent. Staying hydrated, protecting your skin from sun, and following your provider's aftercare help. Your injector can give a realistic maintenance schedule for the specific product and area you had treated.
faqs: Which dermal fillers last the longest?

Biostimulatory fillers like Sculptra (poly-L-lactic acid) and Radiesse (calcium hydroxylapatite) tend to last the longest — often a year to two or more — while hyaluronic-acid lip fillers are usually the shortest-lasting.
Do lip fillers last as long as cheek fillers?
Usually not. Lips move constantly and metabolize filler faster, so lip filler often needs touch-ups sooner than filler placed in more stable areas like the cheeks or jawline.
Can dermal fillers be dissolved?

Hyaluronic-acid fillers can be dissolved with an enzyme called hyaluronidase if you dislike the result or have a complication. Non-HA fillers like Radiesse and Sculptra cannot be dissolved this way, which is one reason product choice matters.

title: How Much Does IV Therapy Cost in Florida? (2026 Price Guide)
h1: How much does IV therapy cost in Florida?
lede: IV therapy is priced per session, and how much you pay depends mostly on the formula in the bag. In Florida, published prices most commonly run about $100 to $400 per session — basic hydration and simple vitamin drips at the lower end, specialty infusions like NAD+ higher. Memberships and packages typically lower the per-session cost.
sections: How IV therapy pricing works

IV drips are billed per session, and the formula drives the price. A basic hydration or electrolyte drip is the least expensive; classic vitamin blends such as a Myers' cocktail sit in the middle; and specialty or high-dose infusions — NAD+, high-dose vitamin C, glutathione add-ons — cost the most. Many IV lounges and med spas also sell add-on boosters (extra vitamins, or anti-nausea and anti-inflammatory medications) that raise the total.
What changes your price

Beyond the formula, price varies with the provider (a physician-supervised clinic may charge more than a walk-in lounge), your location (metro areas like Miami tend to run higher), and whether the service is in-clinic or mobile — at-home mobile IV visits usually add a travel or convenience fee. Memberships, first-visit specials and multi-session packages are the main ways to bring the per-drip cost down.
Getting an accurate quote

IV therapy is a cash-pay wellness service, so insurance does not cover it. Reputable Florida providers list or quote a per-session price and explain what is in each drip. If you plan to go regularly, compare membership and package pricing rather than single-session rates, and confirm the clinic is staffed by licensed medical professionals. faqs: How much is a basic IV drip in Florida?
A basic hydration or simple vitamin drip usually starts near the lower end of the roughly $100 to $400 range at Florida med spas and IV lounges. Specialty infusions such as NAD+ cost more.
Does insurance cover IV therapy?
No — elective IV vitamin and hydration therapy is a cash-pay wellness service and is not covered by insurance. Clinics often offer memberships or packages to reduce the per-session cost.
Why do IV therapy prices vary so much?

The formula is the biggest factor — a simple hydration bag costs far less than a high-dose or specialty infusion. Provider type, location, add-on boosters and whether the drip is mobile or in-clinic also change the price.

title: How Much Does Morpheus8 Cost in Florida? (2026 Price Guide)
h1: How much does Morpheus8 cost in Florida?
lede: Morpheus8 is priced per session and by the area treated. In Florida, published prices for a single facial session most commonly run about $600 to $1,800, with the neck or body costing more. Because a full result usually takes about three sessions, most clinics offer discounted packages.
sections: How Morpheus8 pricing works

Morpheus8 is billed per session, and the two biggest factors are the area treated and how many sessions you buy. A small facial zone costs less than full face-and-neck, and body areas (abdomen, arms, thighs) cost the most because they need more energy and larger tips. Since most people need a series of about three sessions for the full collagen-building effect, clinics commonly sell three- or four-session packages at a lower per-session rate than a single treatment.
What changes your price

Beyond area and session count, price varies with the provider's credentials (a board-certified dermatologist or plastic surgeon usually charges more than an esthetician-run spa), the depth and settings used, and any add-ons like numbing or a combined treatment. Metro markets such as Miami tend to price higher than smaller Florida towns. Introductory offers and memberships are common ways to lower the cost.
Getting an accurate quote

Morpheus8 is cosmetic, so insurance does not cover it. A reputable Florida provider quotes a per-session and package price at a consultation after assessing your skin and mapping the areas. Compare the full-plan cost (per session x sessions), not just a single-session sticker price, and confirm the provider is properly trained on the device. faqs: How much is one Morpheus8 session for the face in Florida?

A single facial Morpheus8 session commonly runs about $600 to $1,800 at Florida med spas and clinics, depending on the area and provider. Neck and body areas cost more, and packages lower the per-session price.
Is Morpheus8 cheaper in a package?

Usually yes. Because a full result typically takes about three sessions, most clinics sell multi-session packages at a lower per-session rate than a single treatment. Ask for package pricing when you compare quotes.
Does insurance cover Morpheus8?
No — Morpheus8 is a cosmetic treatment and is not covered by insurance. Many clinics offer financing or package pricing to spread the cost.

title: What Is Morpheus8? How RF Microneedling Works, Results and Downtime
lede: Morpheus8 is a radiofrequency (RF) microneedling treatment that combines tiny needles with heat to remodel the deeper layers of skin. It is used to tighten mild laxity, smooth texture and soften scarring on the face, neck and body — going deeper than standard microneedling, with a bit more downtime.
sections: How Morpheus8 works

A handpiece drives an array of fine microneedles into the skin and delivers radiofrequency energy from their tips. The needles create controlled micro-injuries that trigger collagen production, while the RF heat remodels tissue in the deeper dermis and, on body areas, the fat layer beneath. That combination — needling plus heat, at an adjustable depth — is what separates Morpheus8 from surface-only microneedling and lets it firm and contour as well as resurface.
What it treats

Morpheus8 is used for mild skin laxity and early sagging, fine lines and wrinkles, rough texture and enlarged pores, and acne or surgical scarring. On the body it is used to tighten areas like the abdomen, arms and knees. It is popular as a step up when creams and standard microneedling have not gone far enough, but short of a surgical lift — it will not replace surgery for significant sagging.
Results, downtime and sessions

Most people need a series of about three sessions spaced four to six weeks apart, with results building over the following months as new collagen forms — so the full effect is gradual, not immediate. Downtime is modest: expect redness, a grid-like or sandpaper texture and sometimes mild swelling for a few days. A numbing cream is applied beforehand to keep the treatment comfortable, and sun protection afterward is important while the skin recovers.
faqs: Is Morpheus8 the same as microneedling?

Not quite. Both use needles to stimulate collagen, but Morpheus8 adds radiofrequency heat and reaches deeper, so it does more for skin laxity and deeper concerns. Standard microneedling is gentler and less expensive, and works well for surface texture and tone.
Does Morpheus8 hurt?

Providers apply a numbing cream first, so most people tolerate it well, describing pressure and warmth more than sharp pain. Comfort varies with the depth and area treated, and body areas can feel more intense than the face.
How long do Morpheus8 results last?

Results build over a few months and can last a year or more, since the treatment stimulates your own collagen. Because skin keeps aging, many people do occasional maintenance sessions to keep the effect.
